en.headline: Man dies after rescue at Peng Chau open-water race
en.dek: Police said a 58-year-old foreign competitor was found unconscious off Tung Wan around noon and died after a helicopter transfer to Eastern Hospital.
body: A 58-year-old foreign man died on Thursday after he was rescued unconscious during an open-water swimming race off Peng Chau, police said.

Officers received a report at 12:21pm that a competitor was suspected of drowning off Tung Wan beach. He was taken first to the Peng Chau clinic and then by a Government Flying Service helicopter to Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital, where he was certified dead. Police said the cause was still being investigated.

The race was the Peng Chau island swim, reported by local outlets to have been organised by the Hong Kong Cross-Harbour Swimming Group, with courses of about 5.5 kilometres, 3.4 kilometres and 1.7 kilometres starting in the morning. A Very Hot Weather Warning remained in force across Hong Kong at the time.
Authorities have not named the man. No other casualties were reported from the race.

zh.headline: 坪洲泳賽外籍男疑遇溺 送院後不治
zh.dek: 警方稱中午約12時21分接報，58歲外籍參賽者在東灣對開昏迷，經直升機送東區醫院後證實不治。
body: 一名58歲外籍男子周四在坪洲參加游泳比賽期間懷疑遇溺，送院後不治。
警方表示，中午12時21分接報，指一名參賽者在坪洲東灣沙灘對開懷疑遇溺並陷入昏迷。他先被送往坪洲診所，再由政府飛行服務隊直升機轉送東區尤德夫人那打素醫院，最終證實死亡。警方指死因仍有待調查。
本地傳媒報道，當日舉行的是坪洲環島泳賽，由香港渡游團舉辦，設約5.5公里、3.4公里及1.7公里賽程，分別於上午起步。事發時天文台酷熱天氣警告仍然生效。
當局未有公布事主姓名。暫無其他參賽者傷亡的消息。
